# Education in Greece
The Greek education system is structured into pre-primary, primary, secondary, and tertiary stages, governed largely by the Ministry of Education. Compulsory education lasts nine years, comprising six years of primary school (Dimotiko) and three years of lower secondary education (Gymnasio), which concludes at age 15. Students automatically progress from primary to lower secondary. Upper secondary education, known as Lyceum, is non-compulsory and lasts three years, culminating in the "Apolytirio Lykeiou" certificate. Admission to higher education requires this certificate and passing the Pan-Hellenic Examinations, a standardized national test that determines university placement.
The secondary system features diverse school types, including General Lyceums (GEΛ), Vocational Lyceums (EPAL), Model, Art, and Music Lyceums, as well as Integrated Special Vocational Gymnasium-Lyceums. Foreign language instruction is mandatory in English for all secondary students, with French or German as optional second languages. The grading system ranges from 1 to 20, and the curriculum emphasizes orientation groups in the third year of high school to allow specialization. Vocational pathways also include apprenticeship programs like the Post-High School Year Apprenticeship Class, which can lead directly to undergraduate studies upon successful completion and examination.
